sonora_ca.name: Sonora
sonora_ca.obs_note: Sonora has no NWS observing station. The readings come from the Green Spring fire-weather station, 12 miles away and about 700 ft lower.

alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 17 at 11:47PM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55
mph expected.

* WHERE...For the Delta, Foothills, Sacramento Valley, and northern
San Joaquin Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds are expected through this
afternoon.

alerts.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 12:38PM PST until November 19 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
* CHANGES...No changes.

* WHAT...Snow. Snow accumulations up to 4 inches below 5000 feet with
4 to 8 inches above 5000 feet including foothill areas west of
Highway 395 and Virginia City.

* WHERE...Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 7 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and the Thursday
morning and evening commutes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A rain and snow mix may limit accumulations on
valley floors until snow levels fall to 4500 feet or less Wednesday
evening.

alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 18 at 3:35PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Las Vegas NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Owens Valley, Death Valley National Park, Esmeralda and
Central Nye County, and Western Clark and Southern Nye County.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Instances
of blowing dust near dry lake beds will be possible and may result
in visibility reductions. Winds will make for difficult driving
conditions for high profile vehicles. Tree limbs could be blown
down and a few power outages may result.
